chunks: As for the right of your mother,

that you know that she carried you where no one carries anyone, she gave you of the fruit of her heart that which no one gives to anyone, and she protected you with all her limbs. She did not mind going hungry while feeding you, being thirsty while giving you drink, being naked while clothing you, being in the sun while shading you, and forsaking sleep for your sake. She protected you from heat and cold, so that you might belong to her. Indeed, you cannot fulfill her gratitude except with the help and success of God.

key_terms.ثَمَرَةُ قَلْبِهَا: fruit of her heart (metaphor for deepest affection/sacrifice)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific rights and sacrifices of a mother according to Shia Islamic teachings?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin (AS) details the mother's rights by enumerating her physical and emotional sacrifices, from the burden of pregnancy to her selfless provision, framing these acts as a profound spiritual debt. This passage underscores that while human effort is necessary, true gratitude (shukr) is ultimately unattainable without divine assistance (tawfiq), a key concept in Shia ethical theology. The text serves as a practical guide for filial piety, linking maternal care directly to one's spiritual standing and reliance on God.

en.william-c-chittick: The right of your mother is that you know that she carried you where no one carries anyone, she gave to you of the fruit of her heart that which no one gives to anyone, and she protected you with all her organs. She did not care if she went hungry as long as you ate, if she was thirsty as long as you drank, if she was naked as long as you were clothed, if she was in the sun as long as you were in the shade. She gave up sleep for your sake, she protected you from heat and cold, all in order that you might belong to her. You will not be able to show her gratitude, unless through God's help and giving success. [1]
